project.description: The Fugaro project this repository belongs to.

gcp_project.description: The GCP project ID of the installation. Optional; the trust anchor that lets a teammate use the installation without running fugaro update (written by fugaro update). Never guessed from the project name.

profile.description: The project layer's profile of the implicit workflow "default", for a file with no workflows: (docs/project-layer.md). Absent: the project's default_profile. Needs fugaro 0.6.0.

author.description: Who a run's commits are authored by: launcher (the person who launched it, as a stated claim — D604) or fugaro (the run's own identity, today's behaviour — D606). The empty value, an explicit null and the absent key all mean fugaro, and the enum carries all four spells for that reason, as budget.mode's does; config.Parse accepts each of them. It is the repository's own opt-in: a repo-only key, which the project layer and a profile may not set. It selects a behaviour and mints no identity — the launcher fills the address from its own local identity and writes it into the run's task (internal/task's Spec.Author). Needs fugaro 0.14.0: an older runner decodes the file strictly and refuses every run of this repository at bootstrap on the key alone, whatever it says, so `fugaro run` and `fugaro update --repo` refuse a base image older than that release rather than launch or deploy a job that dies there.

base_branch.description: A plain git branch name. Git accepts shell metacharacters in ref names; Fugaro does not, because the branch reaches git, Docker build arguments and Cloud Build.

early_draft.description: Open the draft pull request at the first checkpoint push, marked not verified (default true; with git.pr.checkpoints false, at the first verified stage end). False opens it only when the run finishes, for repositories whose host has no drafts. Labels and reviewers are applied only when the PR becomes ready.

checkpoints.description: Push each commit a run makes to its branch within about a minute (after 5 s without a newer one, at most one push a minute, and at once at every stage boundary), fast-forward only, so a container that dies keeps its committed work (default true). With early_draft, the first checkpoint opens the draft pull request, marked not verified. False pushes only at verified stage ends and at the end. Every push to a branch with an open pull request runs its CI: at worst 60 pushes an hour. Fugaro 0.5.1 or later.

auth.description: Where the run's model calls are authenticated. cascade asks for the project's credentials cascade (docs/credentials-service): it is refused with followup.allow_public, needs budget.mode observe or enforce, and is enabled only by the project policy's routing.claude: {via: cascade}, which only the operator can set. Fugaro before 0.10.0 refuses the value.

models.description: A model per stage role; a role left out uses agent.model. With a budget on, each must be an explicit model ID that has a price.

max_output_tokens.description: Per-call output limit by role; 0 is no limit.

max_run_tokens.description: Limit on a whole run's tokens; 0 is none. In a fugaro.yaml it can only tighten the project's ceiling and the default branch's value.

review_rounds.description: Senior review rounds. Unset or 0 takes the resolved rigor mode's own default (poc 1, startup 2, pro 3, critical 5, hotfix 1); a written number replaces it, up or down, within the recipe's bound of 10.

first_line_review.description: A review by the coder's own model, with a fix between, before the senior review. auto: on only when a provider serves the coder and not the reviewer.

first_line_rounds.description: First-line review/fix cycles, counted apart from review_rounds. Unset or 0 takes the resolved rigor mode's own default (poc 1, startup 2, pro 3, critical 3, hotfix 1); a written number replaces it, up or down, within the recipe's bound of 3.

recipe.description: The recipe (task loop) runs use unless fugaro run --recipe names one: .fugaro/recipes/<name>.yaml, the project's fugaro/recipes/<name>.yaml, or the catalog (default, solo, standard, premium, review-only, pick, test-and-fix, lint-fix, run-digest). Fugaro before 0.5.0 refuses this key.

oauth_token.description: The named Claude account (claude_accounts in the local config) this workflow's agent.auth: oauth uses; absent means the repository's default account, the existing claude-oauth-token secret (docs/design/named-oauth-tokens.md). fugaro run --token NAME overrides it per run. The local config's claude_accounts.<name>.allow_data_to must list this repository, checked at launch, not by this schema. Fugaro before 0.6.5 refuses this key. The not clause refuses two names: "default" (the empty value already means it) and bitbucket-token, the one name the credentials bundle reserves for the platform's own git credential (config.ReservedClaudeAccountName, refused by config.Validate in the same words).

compression.description: The context-compression proxy this workflow's model calls route through (docs/design/headroom-compression.md). The key is reserved and refused: the only value this schema admits is "" (off, the default), and the real value is admitted by the same change that implements the proxy. A repository that sets it is refused with "not yet implemented", not as an unknown key.

budget.description: The repository's cost and model policy. The runner reads it from the default branch and merges it with the project's ceiling; it can only tighten. Model prices are not settable here. A null block, mode, cap or list is the same as leaving it out.

mode.description: The strictest mode of the layers wins: enforce, then observe, then off.

per_run_usd.description: A dollar cap per run; the lowest positive cap of the layers wins. 0 sets none. A cap that rounds to less than a millionth of a dollar is refused.

per_day_usd.description: A dollar cap per UTC day for this repository, enforced by the runner (not the database); the lowest positive cap of the layers wins, and a lower cap the owner set in the database wins over it. 0 sets none.

items.description: An explicit model ID, not an alias.

allowed_models.description: The models the run may use; the intersection of the layers' lists.

ab.description: The repository's A/B opt-out (docs/model-ab-testing, D556, D557). A file that writes no ab: block sets nothing; one that writes it may carry ab.rate: 0 alone, which never samples this repository. Every other key of the block — the challengers, the judge model, the daily pair count and the exchange rates — belongs to the project layer, because a repository author who could name a challenger could send that repository's code to a provider the owner opened only to others. The block is closed to them: writing one of those keys is refused here even when it is empty, which the decoder would read as a key that says nothing. Nothing reads these keys to launch a pair before fugaro 0.15.0.

rate.description: Only 0: sampling is the project layer's rate unless this repository turns it off, which is the whole of what a repository may say here.

governance.description: What a run of this repository may spend on one stage, how much review it accepts, and how far one stage may fan out (docs/task-governance/spec.md §2, §5). Every key is a bound whose smaller value is the stricter one, so this block can only tighten what the project layer set (docs/project-layer.md §5); the keys the project layer may loosen are the ones Fugaro ships defaults for (review_ratio, review_floor_calls, max_subagents, stage_budget). A null block, or a key written as null or 0, sets nothing and takes the default. The stages are the run's three spend stages: an artifact run's plan and render steps have no governance budget, so a key naming one is refused.

review_ratio.description: N, the ratio guardrail: review calls above N times the implement stage's calls stop the stage (spec §2). Fugaro's default is 5, and the project layer is the only layer that may loosen it.

review_floor_calls.description: The review-call count below which the ratio is not applied at all, so a short implementation is still reviewed: the bound is max(floor, N x implement calls). Fugaro's default is 20.

max_subagents.description: The most distinct sub-agents one stage may start, concurrently or in total (spec §5). Fugaro's default is 5.

stage_budget.description: A stage's share of the run's budget (G§2). Implement and review are fractions of the per-run cap, review counting the first-line and the senior review together; fix is a fraction of the implement stage's own budget. Fugaro's defaults are 0.7, 0.5 and 0.5.

implement.description: The implement stage's share of the per-run cap. Fugaro's default is 0.7.

review.description: The review stage's share of the per-run cap, first-line and senior review together. Fugaro's default is 0.5.

fix.description: The fix stage's share of the implement stage's own budget, not of the per-run cap. Fugaro's default is 0.5.

stage_tokens.description: A stage's token ceiling, in tokens. Unset by default: a stage with no ceiling of its own is bounded by the run's own agent.max_run_tokens.

implement.description: The implement stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

review.description: The review stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

fix.description: The fix stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

stage_timeout.description: A stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default. The run's workflows.*.timeouts.stage still bounds it, so a stage timeout longer than that is refused at run start, not here.

implement.description: The implement stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

review.description: The review stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

fix.description: The fix stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

tiers.description: What a run of each expectation tier is expected to cost and take, and how far one of its stages may fan out (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, G6). A tier is an expectation and never a cap: the deployed per-run cap stays the ceiling, so an expected_usd above it is an expectation the run still stops at the cap for, and no key here moves a cap. A key written as null or 0 sets nothing and takes the tier's default. Fugaro ships trivial $0.25/10m, small $1/30m, medium $3/90m and large $8/240m, with max_subagents 3 for trivial and small and 5 for medium and large.

trivial.description: The trivial tier's expectation: a copy or text tweak of a few lines. Fugaro's default is $0.25, 10 minutes, 3 sub-agents.

small.description: The small tier's expectation: a single-file feature or bug fix. Fugaro's default is $1, 30 minutes, 3 sub-agents.

medium.description: The medium tier's expectation: a multi-file change with tests. Fugaro's default is $3, 90 minutes, 5 sub-agents.

large.description: The large tier's expectation: a cross-cutting refactor. Fugaro's default is $8, 240 minutes, 5 sub-agents.

followup.description: Who can steer a follow-up run on a Fugaro pull request (design §4.4, §6.1).

trusted.description: Account IDs whose PR comments a follow-up acts on: on GitHub the numeric user ID, on Bitbucket the account_id.

allow_public.description: Allow follow-ups on a public repository, where anyone can comment.

rigor.description: How much cost this repository's runs accept to reduce risk (docs/rigor-modes/spec.md). A default, not a floor: the project layer's defaults.rigor may set both keys too, and the narrowest layer that sets one wins. Fugaro before 0.11.0 refuses the block.

default.description: The mode a run of this repository resolves to when nothing narrower decides. Absent: the project layer's defaults.rigor.default, else Fugaro's own default (pro). Needs fugaro 0.11.0.

areas.description: Named path rules: the mode a run resolves to when the paths it touches match one. Both layers' lists are in effect (a union, not a replacement), the strictest matched rule decides, and a rule is matched with the same doublestar globs workflows.*.rebuild.paths uses. Needs fugaro 0.11.0.

rigorMode.description: A rigor mode, spelled exactly as fugaro's own vocabulary spells it (internal/rigor): poc, startup, pro, critical, hotfix. A near miss ("Poc", "PRO") is refused where it is written, never read as an unknown mode.

rigorArea.description: One rigor.areas rule: a name to print, a doublestar path glob relative to the repository root, and the mode it sets.

name.description: The rule's name, which the run record, the pull request body and fugaro watch print when they say which rule decided. 1 to 40 characters of letters, digits, space, dash, underscore and dot, starting with a letter or a digit.

match.description: A doublestar path glob relative to the repository root, matched against the paths the run changed. The same rule workflows.*.rebuild.paths follows: not empty, not absolute, no ".." component, and a pattern doublestar validates.

mode.description: The mode this rule sets for the paths it matches.

stageFraction.description: A stage's share of a budget, as a fraction. 0 or null sets nothing and takes Fugaro's default, and 1 or more is refused: the per-run cap stays the ceiling whatever a stage is given (G6), so a stage that could spend it whole would be no budget at all.

stageTokens.description: A stage's token ceiling, in tokens; 0 or null sets nothing.

tierLimits.description: One expectation tier's figures (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, G6). Every key is an expectation and never a cap: the deployed per-run cap stays the ceiling whatever is written here. 0 or null sets nothing and takes the tier's default.

expected_usd.description: What a run of this tier is expected to cost, in dollars. 0 or null sets nothing. An expectation above the deployed per-run cap is still only an expectation: the run stops at the cap (G6).

expected_minutes.description: What a run of this tier is expected to take, in minutes. 0 or null sets nothing.

max_subagents.description: How far one stage of a run of this tier may fan out, at most the same 100 governance.max_subagents is bounded by. 0 or null sets nothing.

githubUserID.description: A GitHub numeric user ID, which a rename doesn't change (gh api users/<login> --jq .id).

anyOf.description: A YAML number is compared by value, so its 20-digit bound is approximate; fugaro checks the text.

bitbucketAccountID.description: A Bitbucket account_id, in either form; a user's UUID is not accepted, since comment authors are matched by account_id.

duration.description: Whole days, hours, minutes and seconds, such as 90m, 1h30m or 1d12h. fugaro also accepts any Go duration, such as 1.5h.

profile.description: The project layer's profile this workflow starts from; its own keys override the profile's field by field. Needs fugaro 0.6.0.

job_profile.description: The project policy's job profile this workflow runs on: the Cloud Run job's shape (provider, cpu, memory, task timeout, secret mounts, admission list) selected by name from the published policy. Absent: standard, which every policy that carries profiles must define. It is job_profile and not profile, which names the project layer's workflow template.

base.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
base.description: Removed in 0.7.0: delete it and declare runtimes in mise.toml (docs/base-image-migration.md)

checkout.description: baked (default): a derived image is built per repository and the job runs it. clone: the job runs the installation's base_images.base directly, with no per-repository build or daily check; image.apt, image.setup, image.tools, image.skip_build_scripts, image.key_files and dockerfile are refused, since they would need a build. clone shipped in fugaro 0.9.0: it needs the runner's own blobless-clone support, which ships at fugaro 0.7.5, and a published fugaro-base. A launch is still refused on a job image older than that release. shared: the job runs a shared dependency-layer image — one image per resolved dependency set, holding no repository's source — and the run clones the repository's own source at launch; image.apt, image.tools, image.key_files and image.skip_build_scripts are accepted (they are the layer that image holds), and image.setup and dockerfile are refused, since both would put this repository's own content into an image every repository on the same dependency set runs. It is not shipped yet: no released fugaro builds or refreshes a shared image yet, so validation refuses checkout: shared — declare baked or clone in the meantime.

node.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
node.description: Removed in 0.7.0: declare node in mise.toml ([tools] node = "24") or in image.tools (docs/base-image-migration.md)

jdk.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
jdk.description: Removed in 0.7.0: declare Java in mise.toml ([tools] java = "temurin-25") (docs/base-image-migration.md)

key_files.description: Repository-relative paths, each a file or a directory, that the dependency install reads and the lockfiles do not carry: a patch applied at install time, a vendored toolchain. The derived image checks them out before the source layer, and a change to one rebuilds the image exactly as a lockfile change does. Each entry is one path, as it is: no glob, no backslash, no control character, no leading /, no .. segment, no .git and not the repository root.

lint.description: The check step's gate command (build | test | lint).

fix.description: The check step's autofix command; needs lint, since the gate runs fix, then lint.

render.description: A mode: artifact recipe's render command: repository text, run once, in the checkout, as the agent's user (docs/design/artifact-runs.md §3). Absent, no artifact recipe may run against this workflow.

probe.description: The artifact recipe's optional check on what it rendered: one command, given the outputs directory and the names in its environment. Absent, the recipe's outputs.probe must be none.

env.description: Must not be a variable Fugaro sets or one that changes how the runner, git, a shell, the build or a runtime behaves (config.ReservedEnvPrefixes and config.ReservedEnvNames).

render.description: Bounds the render step alone; absent means min(verify, total - finalize_reserve). The run's own deadline caps it further (docs/design/artifact-runs.md §3).

inputs.description: Caps what a launcher may attach to a run of this workflow (docs/design/artifact-runs.md §4).

max_files.description: How many files may be attached; absent or 0 means 16 (config.DefaultInputFiles).

max_bytes.description: The most ONE attached file may hold; absent or 0 means 256 MiB (config.DefaultInputBytes).

max_total_bytes.description: The most the WHOLE set may hold; absent or 0 means 1 GiB (config.DefaultInputTotalBytes). The runner stages these beside the render's originals, so the memory rule counts them (docs/design/artifact-runs.md §5.2).

anyOf.description: 0 in any form fugaro reads, such as "0", 0d or 0s: no age limit.
At least 1h and at most 90d, which fugaro checks: days or hours, then optional minutes and seconds, such as 14d or 1d12h.
